title: 工業力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Engineering Mechanics II
keywords: Laws of Motion 2.Inertialforces 3.Motion of Mass Points 4.Moment of Inertia 5.Planar Motion of Rigid Body
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn Newton's laws of motion, and (2) learn the fundamentals of dynamics (motion of mass points and rigid bodies against external forces and moments). Since mechanics is the basis of mechanical engineering, it is essential to understanding any courses focused on mechanical engineering. Students will therefore acquire knowledge on topics such as inertia that are necessary for flight dynamics and structural design.
advice: This course covers the basics of the statics and dynamics of objects. We will cover the following topics: 1. Linear motion of mass points 2. Planar motion of mass points 3. Laws of motion 4. Inertialforces 5. The moment of inertia 6. Planar motion of rigid bodies Students will learn the method of analysis of the motion of mass points and rigid bodies by setting up and solving equations of motion through exercises based on the items listed above. Students are required to understand these concepts, solve practice problems, and then cultivate the ability to apply their knowledge to practical problems. In order to do so, exercise-oriented lectures will be conducted and students are required to show their answers on the exercise positively. At the end of each lecture, understanding degree confirmation practice are conducted.
books: Textbooks: Engineering Mechanics, 3rd edition/New edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd. (in Japanese), Reference books: None, Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: Acquisition of "Engineering Mechanics I", Enough skill of mathematics (especially differential and integral calculus, inner and outer products of vectors), Basic knowledge of mechanics (kinematics and moment of force)

activityGoals.body: Be able to set up equations of motion of mass points, and calculate their velocity and position.
Be able to explain laws of motion, and calculate inertial, centripetal, and centrifugal forces.
Be able to calculate moment of inertia.
Be able to set up equations of motion for simple solid bodies.
Be able to solve equations of motion by applying mathematics, and explain dynamic behavior of them.
